summary.text: Paul Hassink is the Republican candidate for the Oklahoma House of Representatives, District 79, in the November 3, 2026 general election, where he faces Democratic incumbent Melissa Provenzano.
An engineer who worked for American Electric Power Service Corp., he was also the Republican nominee for the seat in 2024, when he lost to Provenzano, 54.6% to 45.4%.

paragraphs.text: Paul Hassink was born in Lake Charles, Louisiana, earned a bachelor's degree from the Georgia Institute of Technology in 1979 and a graduate degree from Purdue University in 1980.

According to Ballotpedia, his career included working as an engineer, supervisor, manager and director for American Electric Power Service Corp., and he has been a member of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, CIGRE and the Knights of Columbus.
Hassink won the 2024 Republican primary for District 79, defeating Jenifer Stevens 73.7% to 26.3%, and lost the general election to Provenzano.

In a Ballotpedia survey, he said he is a three-time Republican nominee for the district, a state-appointed member of the Oklahoma Home Inspection Examiner Committee, a City of Tulsa appointee to the Sales Tax Overview Committee and the elected Tulsa County Republican Party state committeeman.

In the survey, Hassink said his campaign messages include rebuilding public education, protecting children from trafficking and abortion, and giving landowners the chance to take part in publicized open-house meetings when a public project affects their property.
